encounters.cc: Worsening gastroesophageal reflux symptoms and retrosternal burning after meals

lines: Worsening gastroesophageal reflux symptoms and retrosternal burning after meals
He reports a 2-year history of retrosternal burning after meals and occasional regurgitation of sour-tasting fluid into his mouth, which is particularly noticeable when lying down at night.
Initially, symptoms occurred once every few weeks but have become almost nightly over the past 6 months.
He occasionally experiences a sensation of food "coming back up" without vomiting and says that sleeping propped up on several pillows provides partial relief.
He denies dysphagia, odynophagia, weight loss, hematemesis, or melena.
He notes that these snacks often worsen his burning sensation, which prompted him to seek medical attention.
He has tried over-the-counter antacids with temporary relief but no lasting improvement.
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (GOLD stage II)
He also has a chronic cough from asthma,.
- Right knee anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (age 35)
He takes for which he uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation twice daily
- Aspirin 81 mg orally daily for cardiovascular prophylaxis
He has no known food allergies.
His father developed "bad heartburn" in his 60s and was told he had a hernia near his stomach.
The patient works as an accountant and spends most of his day at a desk.
He is obese, with a sedentary lifestyle.
He enjoys snacking at night, particularly on ginger crackers and diet lemon-lime soda while reading historical nonfiction.
He does not smoke, drinks alcohol socially,
Vital signs are within normal limits.
Physical examination reveals an overweight man in no acute distress.
Cardiac and lung examinations are normal.
Abdominal examination shows mild epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding.
There is no hepatosplenomegaly or palpable mass.
Rectal examination is normal, and stool is guaiac-negative.
Barium swallow shows a sliding hiatal hernia.
Upper endoscopy demonstrates mild erosive esophagitis without evidence of Barrett esophagus.

encounters.cc: Progressive right knee pain with cracking sensation on movement

lines: Progressive right knee pain with cracking sensation on movement
The patient with post-traumatic osteoarthritis returns for reevaluation of knee symptoms following his recent gastroenterology visit.
He reports a 6-month history of progressive right knee pain, particularly worse when climbing stairs and after prolonged sitting, with a sensation of "cracking" in his knee joint on movement.
- Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (GOLD stage II)
His past medical history is significant for a right anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction 20 years ago following a skiing accident.
- Right knee anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (age 35)
- Albuterol inhaler 90 mcg, 2 inhalations every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol inhaler 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation twice daily
- Aspirin 81 mg orally daily for cardiovascular prophylaxis
- Father with coronary artery disease (myocardial infarction at age 60)
- Older brother with gastric adenocarcinoma (diagnosed age 58)
Smoking: Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2 years ago.
On physical examination, there is mild swelling of the right knee with tenderness on palpation of the medial joint line.
There is no erythema or warmth.
Range of motion is limited by pain at the extremes, and a crepitus is felt during flexion and extension.
Radiographs of the right knee show joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophyte formation at the medial compartment.

lines: Acute exacerbation of right knee pain worsening with activity over the past year
